title: Sherlock: Synthetic-driven config-delta evaluator for batching and cache tradeoffs
creator: Priya Kaur
description: Implement a repeatable, synthetic-driven evaluation harness (codename: Sherlock) that measures latency-vs-quality tradeoffs for batching and KV cache configuration deltas and wires the signals into our regression-monitoring pipeline. The goal is to produce actionable contour maps and rollback thresholds whenever config or model variant changes are proposed, and to provide a fast pre-rollout guardrail for canary decisions.
background: We frequently introduce batching and cache configuration changes to reduce unit cost or improve throughput. Small config deltas can produce non-linear quality regressions for specific slices (short prompts, code completions, multi-turn chat). Current monitoring captures production regressions post-rollout but lacks a fast pre-rollout probe that ties config deltas to expected LQ degradation vs latency gains. Sherlock should synthesize realistic request slices, run controlled comparisons across model+config variants, and emit both human-readable reports and machine signals for Console regression alerts.
success_criteria: Sherlock can run a full config-delta comparison (baseline vs candidate) in under 2 hours for the standard regression suite
Generated tradeoff matrix includes p50/p95/p99 latency, token cost, and LQ metrics for top 10 slices
A regression signal is generated and routed to console-alerts when weighted LQ delta exceeds 2% and latency gain exceeds 15%
Integration test with canary flow triggers blocking rollback when threshold breached in staging
tasks: Design synthetic slice set: short prompts, dialogue history, code, instruction-following, and embeddings similarity cases
Implement Sherlock harness runner and scheduler (k8s CronJob + ephemeral cluster option)
Instrument per-slice metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, e2e generation time, new LQ composite score, hallucination rate
Add config matrix generator: microbatch sizes, pack shapes, KV TTLs, eviction strategies, prefix-merge heuristics
Run initial matrix sweep against two model variants and collect artifacts
Wire outcomes into regression-monitoring ingest with schema and alert thresholds
Create Console report template and playbook for run interpretation
Add a lightweight canary gate for staging rollouts based on Sherlock signals
testing_plan: Unit tests for harness orchestration and result serialization
Synthetic end-to-end runs on 10 config deltas with small clusters (smoke)
Full sweep regression on nightly infra against long-tail slices (baseline comparison)
Adversarial prompts to stress KV expiry and prefix-caching behavior
Manual QA: PM + ML Eng reviews of top-3 false-positive/false-negative cases
rollout_plan: Phase 1 - internal alpha: run Sherlock on dev clusters for 2 weeks, iterate on slice weighting
Phase 2 - staging canaries: integrate with canary orchestration; block if rule fires
Phase 3 - automated premerge: expose a lightweight quick-run in CI for small config changes
Phase 4 - GA: ship as part of runtime-1.22 with Console integration and playbook
monitoring_alerts: LQ_delta_alert: fires when weighted LQ delta > 2% AND latency gain > 15%
Slice_outlier_alert: fires when any slice sees >5% absolute drop in preferred LQ metric
Data_drift_alert: fires when input token distribution deviates from lab slice baseline >10%
Execution_timeout_alert: runs taking >4 hours are failed and flagged for infra debugging
